$comment: The FLSA floor. Every other file in this folder is a rate that sits ON TOP of this one: an employer owes the HIGHEST of the federal, state and local minimum wages that cover a given hour of work, never the one printed closest to hand. That 'highest applicable' rule is DOL's own, quoted in the sources below, and it is the single rule minimumWage() in src/minimum-wage.ts implements.

standard.coverage: Employees of enterprises with at least $500,000 in annual business volume, plus individually covered employees engaged in interstate commerce -- 29 U.S.C. 203(s), 206(a).
standard.note: Unchanged since 2009-07-24, the last step of the Fair Minimum Wage Act of 2007. There is no federal indexation mechanism: the figure moves only when Congress moves it.

tippedEmployeeThreshold.note: 29 U.S.C. 203(t): an employee who customarily and regularly receives MORE than $30 a month in tips.

tipped.note: The employer must make up any shortfall: cash wage plus tips actually received must reach $7.25/hr for every hour worked. A tip credit is available only if the employee was informed of it and retains all tips (except a valid tip pool).

youthAndTraining.label: Youth opportunity wage
youthAndTraining.eligibility: Employees under 20 years old, for the first 90 CONSECUTIVE CALENDAR days after initial employment -- 29 U.S.C. 206(g). Not 90 days worked, and not renewable by re-hiring.
youthAndTraining.note: Several states republish this same federal 90-day wage rather than legislating their own; a handful (Iowa, Michigan, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Nebraska) set a DIFFERENT training figure, which is carried in that state's own file.

otherFederalMinimums.$comment: Federal minimum wages that are NOT the FLSA floor. Carried because a payroll system that only knows $7.25 will underpay on a covered federal contract -- and, in 2026 specifically, will OVERpay if it is still applying the revoked Executive Order 14026 rate.

executiveOrder13658.coverage: Contracts entered into, renewed or extended BEFORE 2022-01-30 that remain covered by EO 13658 (Establishing a Minimum Wage for Contractors, 2014).
executiveOrder13658.note: DOL published the 2026 rate change notice on 2026-02-09 (91 FR, 'Minimum Wage for Federal Contracts Covered by Executive Order 13658, Notice of Rate Change in Effect'), raising the rate to $13.65 and the tipped rate to $9.55 effective 2026-05-11.

executiveOrder14026.note: EO 14026 (2021) had set a $17.75 contractor minimum wage for 2025, indexed annually. Executive Order 14236 of 2025-03-14 revoked it; DOL stopped enforcing EO 14026 and 29 CFR part 23 and has published no rate for it since. A REAL TRAP for a payroll system carrying a stale 2025 table: EO 14026's rate is not merely frozen, it no longer applies at all, and covered older contracts fall back to EO 13658's much lower $13.65.

section14cSubminimum.note: Section 14(c) certificates (workers with disabilities), 14(a) student-learner / full-time-student certificates, and the messenger and learner programs all permit sub-minimum wages set individually by certificate, not by a published rate. Nothing in this database asserts a figure for them; a payroll system handling a 14(c) employer must read that employer's own certificate.

highestApplicableRule: DOL, on its own State Minimum Wage Laws page: where federal, state and local minimum wage laws all cover the same employee, the employer must pay the HIGHEST of the applicable rates. This database therefore stores each level separately and never pre-merges them.

knownGaps: Special federal minimum wages set by certificate (14(c), student learners, apprentices, messengers) carry no figure here -- they are per-certificate, not per-jurisdiction.
The Service Contract Act and Davis-Bacon Act prevailing wages are a different mechanism entirely (per-contract wage determinations, not a single rate) and are out of scope for this database.
American Samoa's FLSA floor is NOT $7.25 -- it is a set of 18 industry-specific rates, carried in territories/AS-2026.json.
